s1.syndrome_frame: Acute chest pain with pleuritic and intermittent characteristics, associated with diaphoresis and elevated troponin levels, in a young adult with a recent history of ulcerative colitis
salient_findings: Pleuritic pain worsened by sitting forward
Extensive patchy late gadolinium enhancement on cardiac magnetic resonance imaging
key_facts: Started mesalazine 3 weeks prior to admission
No family history of cardiovascular disease
ECG showed sinus rhythm with benign early repolarization
Negative serum viral and autoantibody screens
Transthoracic echocardiography showed borderline low systolic function
Cardiac magnetic resonance imaging demonstrated mild systolic dysfunction and hypokinesia of the anterolateral and inferolateral segments

shortlist.label: Myopericarditis
shortlist.why_kept: Pleuritic chest pain, elevated troponin, and patchy late gadolinium enhancement on CMR suggest myocardial inflammation

shortlist.label: Viral myocarditis due to coxsackievirus
shortlist.why_kept: Elevated troponin, mild systolic dysfunction, and myocardial edema on CMR are consistent with viral myocarditis

shortlist.label: Acute coronary syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Elevated troponin and chest pain are consistent with acute coronary syndrome, although the patient's young age and lack of cardiovascular risk factors make this less likely

shortlist.label: Pericarditis
shortlist.why_kept: Pleuritic chest pain and elevated C-reactive protein suggest pericardial inflammation, although the absence of pericardial effusion on echocardiography makes this less likely

shortlist.label: Giant cell myocarditis
shortlist.why_kept: Elevated troponin, mild systolic dysfunction, and patchy late gadolinium enhancement on CMR are consistent with giant cell myocarditis, a rare but potentially life-threatening condition

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation of sharp, central chest pain that worsens with movement, along with elevated troponin and C-reactive protein levels, and the findings on cardiac magnetic resonance imaging (CMR) demonstrating mild systolic dysfunction, hypokinesia, and extensive patchy late gadolinium enhancement, are consistent with myopericarditis. The absence of pericardial effusion does not rule out this diagnosis, as it can be a feature of the disease, especially in its early stages or with partial involvement.

rejected.label: Viral myocarditis due to coxsackievirus
rejected.why: Negative serum viral screens make this less likely

rejected.label: Acute coronary syndrome
rejected.why: The patient's age, lack of cardiovascular risk factors, and the pattern of troponin elevation and CMR findings are not typical for acute coronary syndrome

rejected.label: Pericarditis
rejected.why: While some symptoms could suggest pericarditis, the CMR findings of myocardial involvement (hypokinesia, late gadolinium enhancement) point more towards myopericarditis

rejected.label: Giant cell myocarditis
rejected.why: This condition is rare and typically presents with more severe and rapid progression of heart failure, which is not seen in this patient
